Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

opinion noun

also view, point of view, in my opinion, what’s your opinion?, difference of opinion, give an opinion

classical

Ter. Ph. 454: quot hominēs, tot sententiae
Cic. Att. 7.13a.3: vir meā sententiā magnus
Traupman 21, 354

sententia, sententiae f.

noun, first declension

opinion, view, judgement

In my opinion: meā sententiā (Cic. Att. 7.13a.3; Traupman 21, 354) or meā quidem sententiā (Cic. de Or. 1.20). To give one’s opinion: sententiam dīcere (Traupman 177, 354). “What’s your opinion?” is quid tibi vidētur? or quid cēnsēs? (see seem, think).

Other words

  • opīniō, opīniōnis f. — a belief, an impression, what one supposes (often against the facts); expectation; reputation

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Sen. Ep. 13.4: saepius opīniōne quam rē labōrāmus; Cic. Fam. 14.23.1: opīniōne celerius

    Lewis & Short: “opinion, supposition, conjecture, imagination, fancy, belief”. Ut opīniō mea fert, as I believe (Cic. Fam. 1.9.22); opīniōne celerius, sooner than expected; and the opinion others hold of someone, his reputation.

  • jūdicium, jūdiciī n. — judgement, a considered opinion

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 5.1.4: meō jūdiciō; Traupman 354

Examples

  • Quot hominēs, tot sententiae; suus cuique mōs.

    So many men, so many opinions; everyone has his own way.Ter. Ph. 454

  • Labiēnus, vir meā sententiā magnus

    Labienus, a great man in my opinionCic. Att. 7.13a.3

  • saepius opīniōne quam rē labōrāmus

    we suffer more often from what we imagine than from what isSen. Ep. 13.4

See also think, agree, idea, seem.
